Any field written as { "en": "…", "km": "…" } is bilingual — fill both. An empty string means 'not supplied yet', and the site hides that item rather than showing a blank.

khmer._readme: The Khmer site. `published` is the launch switch: with it false, every /km/… page is still built and reachable by URL — so the Khmer copy can be read and reviewed — but it is not offered to visitors. The EN/ខ្មែរ switch disappears from the header and the mobile drawer, no hreflang alternates are emitted, the /km pages carry `noindex` and are kept out of the sitemap. Nothing is deleted: km.json and every { en, km } field stay as they are, so flipping this to true publishes Khmer again. `useKhmerNumerals` decides whether the Khmer site renders numbers in Khmer numerals (០១២៣) or Arabic (0123) — the open decision on the 'Numerals' row of the Khmer Glossary sheet. Set it once here and every date, statistic and figure follows.

features._readme: Switch whole sections and pages off without deleting their content — useful for launching before every section is signed off. `network` is OFF pending review: the Asia Network section claimed APP is the Cambodia practice of the Twin Pillars group (Open Question #1), sourced from twinpillars.asia rather than from APP. With the switch off, the section, its nav entry, its page and the '6 Asian markets' statistic all disappear together; network.json and the section component stay in place, so confirming the relationship in writing is a one-line flip back to true. `news` is OFF for launch — the nav entries, /news and every article page disappear; the articles stay in src/content/blog/. `holidays` is OFF: the 'Public holidays · office closed' block at the foot of the contact section is hidden, and the dates stay in holidays.json. `partners` controls the 'Our Partners' block at the foot of /leadership — set it to false and the block disappears; the people stay in partners.json.

images._readme: Photography, as paths inside the public/ folder — e.g. "/images/hero.jpg" for the file public/images/hero.jpg. Leave a value empty and the design falls back to its plain dark treatment, which looks deliberate; it never renders a broken image. Use owned or licensed photography only. Suggested sizes: hero 2400×1400, about 1600×1000, og 1200×630.

seo._readme: ogImage is the picture shown when a page is shared on Facebook, Telegram or LinkedIn. Leave it empty until a real 1200x630 image exists in public/images/ — an og:image pointing at a missing file is worse than none. Then set it to e.g. "/images/og-default.jpg".
